stemMd: A neutral atom has electron arrangement 2,8,1. Which simple ion is it most likely to form?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A +1 ion by losing one electron

options.label: B
options.textMd: A +7 ion by gaining seven electrons

options.label: C
options.textMd: A −8 ion by losing eight electrons

options.label: D
options.textMd: A neutral ion by losing its nucleus

options.label: E
options.textMd: A −1 ion by losing one electron

explanationMd: The atom has one electron outside a filled inner shell. Losing that valence electron gives a stable closed-shell configuration and leaves one more proton than electrons, so the ion has charge +1. Check charge by subtracting electron number from proton number.

distractorRationale.e: Losing a negative electron makes charge more positive, not negative.
distractorRationale.b: Gaining electrons makes charge more negative.
distractorRationale.d: Removing the nucleus does not produce a chemically meaningful neutral ion.
distractorRationale.c: The charge sign is inconsistent with electron loss.
